answer: One island beacon station per identity locks a 70-credit bond and files a key-signed beacon flash log. Flashes follow a comet passage; the auditor recomputes that island schedule from the comet ephemeris, burning it for a missing, mistimed, or reused flash. A rented-keeper ring fails because copied timestamps match no second island ephemeris and carry the wrong key. The first station pays 22; the kth from one source pays 22+5(k-1), so the 1000th pays 5017 and 1000 fakes pay 2519500 plus 70000 locked, no discount. An honest keeper files once, pays 22, and recovers it after a clean epoch.
